question: Which percentage-grant bases and funding options ship in release 1?
recommendation: FixedAmount and Percentage of available-to-recommend only (fixed at approval), ResidualSweep for closing grants, one default cash-first waterfall; defer other bases, weights, templates and recurring percentages.
alternatives: All five bases (as written);Fixed amounts only (no closing-grant support)
rationale: R1 has one pool or cash sweep (report 17), so other bases have no distinct meaning (SPF-FIN-006).

question: Which financial statements are generated in Unbound and which in the sponsor ERP?
recommendation: Unbound: DAF-program trial balance, fund statements, Schedule D bridge, DAF disclosures. ERP: entity-wide statements using the summarized export.
alternatives: Unbound produces full entity statements (needs operating data);ERP produces everything (loses fund-level drill-down)
rationale: Avoid two books of record for operating data (RCF-FIN-008).

question: Confirm XRJ-ERP-002 (no native budgeting) over the adopted wording of RR-UNB-ACC-014-r1?
recommendation: Yes; adopt RR-UNB-ACC-014-r2.
alternatives: Keep native budgeting
rationale: Consistency (SPF-FIN-004).

question: Must the advisor re-consent when the sponsor changes only the funding source of an unchanged grant?
recommendation: No; notify only. Consent only for recipient, amount or timing changes.
alternatives: Always require consent (as written)
rationale: Funding source is within sponsor exclusive legal control (IRC §4966(d)(2)).

question: Remove native rebalancing, trade staging and pre/post-trade compliance (UNB-INV-031)?
recommendation: Remove; managers/custodians perform these; oversight via RR-UNB-INV-019-r1 drift monitoring and manager reviews.
alternatives: Keep as conditional capability for self-managed pools
rationale: XRJ-INV-003 and XIF-INV-011 (duplication).

question: Must staff accounting workbenches (close, reconciliation) be phone-first, or WCAG 2.2 AA with reflow only?
recommendation: WCAG 2.2 AA including reflow for all surfaces; phone-first design only for donor/advisor journeys and approvals.
alternatives: Phone-first everywhere (as written)
rationale: Accessibility unchanged; design cost reduced (SPF-FIN-012).

question: Is one accrual (GAAP) book per entity sufficient, with other bases derived?
recommendation: Yes.
alternatives: Parallel cash and accrual books
rationale: XID-INV-005 puts Schedule D on audited basis; derived reports cover other needs.

question: May a deep-review renewal (and the routine diligence result) be approved by the sponsor's versioned deterministic policy with no human sign-off when all evidence is current and passing?
recommendation: Yes, under board delegation (OD-01), with independent after-the-fact sampling (UNB-XIN-CLM-005) and guardrail metrics.
alternatives: Human sign-off on every renewal (~8,333 h per 10k accounts [D]);Human sign-off only on renewals with changed evidence
rationale: Grant approval authority is already delegable (REQ-X-017); renewal of a factual verification is lower-stakes than grant approval.

question: May sponsor-originated verified corrections (e.g. a confirmed new legal address) update the common registry for all sponsors?
recommendation: Allow only public-source-verifiable facts, re-verified by the platform from the public source, never the sponsor's private evidence (consistent with RCD-029).
alternatives: No sponsor-derived updates;Full sharing under contract
rationale: Improves common evidence quality without leaking private data.

question: What maximum age and invalidation triggers apply to reuse of human false-positive sanctions dispositions?
recommendation: Reuse until subject identity attributes or the list entry change, with a counsel-set maximum age (e.g. 12 months [A]).
alternatives: No reuse;Reuse without maximum age
rationale: Keeps strict-liability screening at every point while removing repeat adjudication.

question: Should grants to charities with a verified ACH destination be paid by ACH by default, with checks by exception?
recommendation: Yes; report 17 already sets 'ACH by default, check otherwise'; make it explicit and measure check share.
alternatives: Donor choice of rail;Check default
rationale: grt.md §8 identifies eliminating checks as a main saving; checks drive positive pay, outreach and escheat work.

question: Defer 50-state charity registration/standing acquisition and state-rule tracking until a decision consumes them?
recommendation: Defer; grantee state standing is not a grantor obligation (XRA-015) and was rejected as a gate (XRJ-NPG-002).
alternatives: Build now as optional sponsor signal
rationale: No R1 decision consumes it; ~80 h per 10k accounts [A] plus build cost.

question: In release 1 (one sponsor, platform operated for that sponsor), does any party need a SOC 2 (or SOC 1) report on the platform, and if not, which SOC2-family requirements become conditional?
decision_owner: Product owner with sponsor CFO and CPA
recommendation: Keep SOC2-family evidence engineering (by-product evidence, integrity, missing-evidence detection) — it serves the sponsor's own audit and bank/custodian due diligence. Defer the SOC 2 system description, CUEC/CSOC and audit-period work until a user entity (second sponsor, partner) or counterparty contract requires a report.
alternatives: Pursue SOC 2 Type II from launch (~200 h/yr [A] plus auditor fees);SOC 1 Type II only for fund accounting if the sponsor auditor relies on it
rationale: SOC 2 is a market/contract expectation, not law; its consumers are user entities that R1 does not have (17 §1). The evidence layer has value regardless; the report ceremony does not yet.

question: Should delegated customer roles (advisors, viewers) be recertified annually with auto-suspension, or end on events with an annual no-action notice?
recommendation: Event-driven expiry (parent change, explicit expiry, inactivity) plus annual informational notice; keep quarterly workforce recertification.
alternatives: Keep annual recertification with auto-suspend;Annual recertification without auto-suspend
rationale: Removes ~0.3 donor interactions per account per year [A] and advisor lockouts (XIF-ADV-018) while AUTH-I2 already ends derived rights automatically.

question: Which control catalog is authoritative, and are UNB-CTRL (90, templated), UNB-SCTRL (46), CTL (54) and TVCTL (14) merged into one register?
recommendation: One register per MON-001 with UNB-SCTRL and CTL/TVCTL entries merged by objective; retire the 30x3 templated UNB-CTRL matrix as authoritative (keep as a domain index view).
alternatives: Keep all catalogs with a crosswalk;Adopt UNB-CTRL as master and map others
rationale: Templated matrix rows (same three objectives per domain) are not executable controls; four catalogs multiply ownership, attestation and mapping work.

question: How are segregation-of-duties and independence requirements met at release-1 staffing (mandatory rotation, CISO reporting line, reviewer per control, reconciliation outside payment chain)?
recommendation: Keep engine-enforced SoD and reconciliation outside the payment chain (outsourced accountant if needed); replace mandatory rotation with enforced leave where >=2 trained staff and anomaly analytics otherwise; give CISO direct committee access rather than a reporting line; independent reviewer only for key and manual controls (RR-OPS-004-r1).
alternatives: Apply all as written (requires larger staff);Outsource independent review entirely
rationale: Independence must be genuine, not nominal; requirements written for large organisations produce paper compliance at small scale.

question: Should REQ-X-058..077 (and the landscape-wave outcome/hypothesis records) be reclassified as a non-normative capability index, with tests attached only to their carrier records?
recommendation: Yes. Keep each ID as an index entry linking to carriers (report section 2); keep deferred status where the feature is out of R1.
alternatives: Keep both layers normative (status quo);Delete the scope records (loses history)
rationale: Scope statements have no acceptance criteria; carriers do. Two layers double trace and test work.

question: Which reconciliation window and outcome set apply to reconsideration, and which record survives?
recommendation: UNB-XIN-CLM-001 survives; window default 60 days (RCD-046); outcomes {Upheld, Reversed, Modified, Withdrawn, Referred}; response 30 days.
alternatives: 90-day default (more donor-friendly, slower closure);Keep three records
rationale: One record removes contradictory notices; 60 days matches the only decided value.

question: What is the default statement notification and paper policy (RR-REQ-X-032-r1)?
recommendation: Generate and publish every period; notify by quarterly digest by default plus correction alerts; monthly notification as donor opt-in; paper on request or without e-consent, free as an accommodation.
alternatives: Monthly notification by default (status quo);Quarterly statements only
rationale: Statements are sponsor policy (report 09 line 33); generation is free, notifications are friction.

question: May affiliation attestation (UNB-XIN-CRM-002) be event-driven with an embedded prefilled confirmation instead of a separate annual attestation?
recommendation: Yes: capture at onboarding; update on signals; prefilled confirmation in the next session after 12 months; outreach only if absent and a recommendation is pending.
alternatives: Annual outreach to all holders;Capture once only
rationale: Keeps the screening input current without calendar outreach; detection still runs on every recommendation (TVCTL-14).

question: Should continued-holding re-review (UNB-RCN-WF-030) be event-driven rather than every 12 months?
recommendation: Event-driven triggers plus automated reconfirmation outreach every 12 months without staff review; human only at disposition.
alternatives: Keep 12-month human re-review
rationale: Change-driven principle (report 09 line 8).

question: May the sponsor board delegate routine fund acceptance to a deterministic policy (RR-ADM-003-r1), and may intake prefill from held facts (RR-ADM-002-r1)?
recommendation: Build the deterministic tier now; outcome AcceptRecommended for batch A4 approval until delegation is recorded (same pattern as RCD-005).
alternatives: Human acceptance of every fund
rationale: Acceptance of a standard fund under published terms is a policy match; humans add value only on non-standard cases.

question: Apply the RecurringObligation register (UNB-XIN-ADV-001 part 1) to all servicing classes in release 1?
recommendation: Yes, as an inventory with legal basis class and interactions per account-year; keep DigitalMinimal budget enforcement deferred.
alternatives: Keep fully deferred
rationale: It is the only device that exposes convention-driven recurring work.

question: Move research tasks and open hypotheses (UNB-GAP-001..009, UNB-COM-001, UNB-HYP-003/009) to an evidence backlog with owners and due dates?
recommendation: Yes; GAP-001 shadow replay first because it replaces the economic model's assumed exception rate and minutes.
alternatives: Leave in requirement files
rationale: They have no system behaviour.

question: When routine payment release is performed by the board-delegated deterministic gate, does the gate count as the 'releaser' for SoD purposes, so that PA-2/NotReceived resolution needs two humans (not three distinct people)?
decision_owner: Audit & risk committee with counsel and external auditor
recommendation: Yes, provided the gate is a published, independently approved policy version and the two human approvers did not author or publish it.
alternatives: No (treat gate as no releaser → still 2 humans); No (require 3 humans always).
rationale: Determines whether the payment-chain floor is 4 or 5 named holders.

question: May the sponsor's DoA name contracted or fractional individuals (not employees) for A4 decisions (exception grants, sanctions true-match, treasury exception release), and in what appointment form?
recommendation: Allow only for individuals appointed by board resolution as officers/agents of the sponsor with conflict attestations; vendor staff without such appointment stay below A3 (UNB-XIN-CLM-008).
alternatives: Employees only; any vendor staff under contract.
rationale: Fractional and solo-sponsor structures depend on it.

question: Coverage depth for reserved decision classes during the December 24–January 2 window: single absence (4 holders) or double absence (5 holders)?
recommendation: Double absence for payment chain during the year-end window; single absence otherwise.
alternatives: Single always; double always.
rationale: December is the peak (economic-model §3); absence correlation is highest then.

question: Default operating structure for the first sponsor.
recommendation: Solo sponsor on shared services (S1) with outsourced reconciliation, assurance, counsel and tax.
alternatives: Fractional (S2); AI-native core team (S3); conventional (S4).
rationale: Lowest fixed cost at 1k–10k accounts while keeping legal control.

question: Default assignment mode per case kind.
recommendation: See report 'Assignment models' default table (exception grants SkillBased; succession CradleToGrave; service StickyRelationship for advisor-distributed sponsors else RoundRobin; fraud Escalation-only).
alternatives: Sponsor-chosen only.
rationale: Defaults reduce configuration cost.

question: Independent reconciler below 10k accounts: outsourced firm or internal person outside the payment chain?
recommendation: Outsourced monthly review plus daily automated matching, until workload exceeds ~0.5 FTE.
alternatives: Internal hire.
rationale: alternatives §8 notes outsourced review may cost less at very small scale.

question: Which cost targets, by operating model and servicing class, replace the single $258 reference?
recommendation: Keep open. Replace recommended cost bands with base versus adversarial ranges from the executed model; state each target with the SLA level it buys and who bears acquisition cost; decide SPD-ADV-001 first (SPR-ADV-002, SPF-ADV-003). SPD-ADV-001 and SPD-ADV-004 are now decided; use report 24 figures for OM3-OM5 (customer total cost and Unbound vendor cost separately), not the pooled figures in reports 06-09.
alternatives: Keep $258 as a single target;Adopt $100 platform-wide;No target until measured
rationale: Executed model: $258 reachable by lean models at ≥100k but not by baseline levers at P50; $100 unreachable for full-service at P50 up to 5M; $10 unreachable up to 5M.

question: How are small balances priced: minimum fee, DigitalMinimal low fee, employer sponsorship, or disclosed cross-subsidy?
recommendation: DigitalMinimal class funded by employer fee plus modest asset fee or a disclosed cross-subsidy from balances above a threshold; retain minimum fees only with a cost basis (UNB-SMP-ECN-001). Not an R1 model.
alternatives: $100 minimum as today;Subscription only;Serve at a loss as a channel
rationale: Marginal cost $5-24 vs revenue $9-30 at 0.60%; employer $12 alone never breaks even; asset tiers already cross-subsidise heavily.

question: Should platform pricing have a per-sponsor component in addition to per-account fees?
recommendation: DECIDED (provisional, product owner, 2026-11-24): yes, as a software licence. (A) a per-account licence fee by servicing class and (B) a per-sponsor tenant fee. No decision-team or staffing charge while Unbound is software-only (SPD-ADV-004); the fee model keeps a typed list of components so service components can be added later (UNB-SMP-ECN-004). Modelled cost-recovery floors at OM3@1M: A $10.96/account, B $52,000/sponsor [D, theoretical]. Price levels and margin remain with the CFO and commercial lead.
alternatives: Per-account only;Tiered per-account by sponsor size
rationale: accounts_per_sponsor is the #1 tornado driver in platform models; sponsor-level cost ~$19/acct at 5k accounts/sponsor. The per-sponsor decision team floor (2.5 FTE [A]) is fixed cost per sponsor, so it cannot be recovered fairly by a per-account fee alone.

question: How is December and incident surge capacity procured (seasonal staff, pre-contracted qualified reviewer bench, lead time)?
recommendation: Pre-contract a qualified reviewer and ops bench with ≤5-day activation, sized from the forecast; promote giving plans to shift December arrivals.
alternatives: Seasonal hires only;Accept December SLA breach;Deferral windows
rationale: Model: p90 exception wait exceeds a 5-day SLA in normal Decembers even with 50% seasonal staff; ops floor is the weakest point in simultaneous failures.

question: When complex-asset processing is outsourced, may the vendor fee be charged to the fund, and is that a saving?
recommendation: Charge to fund only as a disclosed, donor-affirmed, cost-based service charge; never report the bearer shift as an operating saving.
alternatives: Absorb in sponsor operating cost;Charge without affirmation
rationale: Model OM2-OM5 move ~$17/acct of complex-asset cost to funds; moving work is not elimination.

question: Is one explicit grouped acknowledgment, with each representation shown verbatim and one evidence record per representation, acceptable evidence for grant affirmations?
recommendation: Option A: yes, except for any representation counsel requires to stand alone.
alternatives: A grouped; B individual checkboxes (current UNB-UI-S-003); C grouped with standalone pledge representation
rationale: The daf-landscape sponsor decision WL-06/D9 permits grouping and keeps evidence distinct. Grant recommendation is the most frequent customer journey.

question: May donor identity proofing be risk-based, with a document and selfie step only when database verification fails or risk is elevated?
recommendation: Yes for release 1 individuals funding by ACH, wire or check from US accounts. Use the document step for entities, complex assets and failed matches.
alternatives: A risk-based; B document step for all; C none beyond bank validation
rationale: XRJ-BNK-001 rejects donor CIP. Bank account validation already binds identity to an account.

question: Above which fund balance band, if any, should advisory-privilege holders re-attest affiliations annually rather than only at onboarding and on change?
recommendation: Merge into SPD-ENT-004 (SPF-ADV-017).
alternatives: A band; B annual for all; C onboarding and change only
rationale: Proportionality. The excess-benefit gate needs the affiliation graph but not annual friction for small funds.

question: When a new Policy Pack version is published, does it auto-apply to attested sponsors after a notice and objection window, or require re-attestation?
recommendation: Auto-apply only strictly tightening pack changes, shadow-evaluated against the sponsor's history and confirmed by the sponsor; any relaxing change needs affirmative sponsor adoption (SPR-ADV-001).
alternatives: A auto-apply; B re-attest always; C hybrid (recommended)
rationale: Legal changes must not wait on sponsor action. Discretionary changes remain under sponsor control (IRC §4966(d)(2) control rests with the sponsor).

question: Default statement cadence: monthly (REQ-X-032) or quarterly with monthly on request (RCD-020 recommendation)?
recommendation: Merge into SPD-ENT-003 (SPF-ADV-017).
alternatives: A monthly; B quarterly; C annual plus on-demand
rationale: Print/mail and rendering cost scale with cadence. No sourced evidence of donor demand for monthly in this pass (unverified).

question: Who bears liability for an error in platform-maintained Policy Pack content that a sponsor adopted by attestation?
recommendation: Allocate in the sponsor contract responsibility matrix (REQ-X-064). The platform warrants the review process, not legal outcomes, and the sponsor retains exclusive legal control.
alternatives: A platform warranty; B sponsor bears all; C contractual allocation (recommended)
rationale: The sponsor holds legal control and the platform supplies reviewed defaults.

question: What is the initial executive KPI set?
recommendation: SPM-001, SPM-002, SPM-003, SPM-004, SPM-006, SPM-008 and SPM-009, each with its counter-metric. No composite score.
alternatives: A minimal set (recommended); B full ECO-022 overview
rationale: Each supports a named decision. The overview metrics document lists the initial executive set as an open decision.

question: What small-group suppression threshold applies to every cross-sponsor benchmark?
recommendation: Use the UNB-XIN-ECO-021 threshold (at least 5 contributing sponsors) for all cross-sponsor metrics, plus a dominance rule [A].
alternatives: A 5 sponsors; B 10 sponsors; C no benchmarks in release 1
rationale: One rule for all benchmarks.

question: Which segment is Unbound's primary competitive entry point: D2C small-balance donors, the advisor channel, or community-foundation/independent-sponsor administration?
recommendation: Treat CF/independent-sponsor administration as the leading hypothesis to test (largest documented cost gap and observed switching), but do not commit until CF requirements (external GL, non-DAF fund types) are scoped and priced; keep D2C small-balance out.
alternatives: D2C small-balance (weak: access exists, tax headwind);Advisor channel (strong incumbents; R1 excludes advisor-managed accounts);Embedded/API sponsor-of-record (Endaoment, Daffy already live)
rationale: Evidence in SPF-CMP-002 and SPF-CMP-004; R1 as proposed (one reference sponsor, D2C + advisor delegation) matches none of the evidenced gaps well.

question: Should Unbound commit to publishing measured service levels (turnaround P50/P90 by rail, response times) and WCAG conformance to donors and charities?
recommendation: Yes, once measured; publish only measured figures with method and period.
alternatives: Internal SLOs only;Publish targets rather than measurements
rationale: No top-20 sponsor publishes either (SPF-CMP-008); publishing unmeasured targets would replicate the 'instant approval' problem (SPR-CMP-001).

question: Release-1 grant-payment rail: sponsor-originated ACH, or a networked rail partner (Chariot, PayPal Grant Payments) as the sponsor's agent?
recommendation: Prefer a networked rail adapter acting as the sponsor's agent for charity reach, keeping sponsor-controlled funds flow (UNB-XIN-OTH-003); retain own-ACH as fallback.
alternatives: Own ACH only (higher charity onboarding friction);Multiple rails from day one (integration cost)
rationale: Competitors' charity-side networks are superior (SPF-CMP-006); report 05 recommends partnering (unbound:requirements/reconciliation/2026-11-23/05-COMPETITIVE-COVERAGE-MATRIX.md:47).

question: Should any external competitive claim require an evidence grade of verified-documented, including logged-in verification for capability-absence claims?
recommendation: Yes: no 'only/first provider' claim without logged-in verification and dated evidence.
alternatives: Allow claims on public-page evidence with caveat
rationale: Census ND means not found on public pages (SPF-CMP-003); misleading-claim risk.

question: How are per-account cost targets defined (cost layer, bearer, scale, servicing class) and is $10 a marginal or fully allocated goal?
recommendation: Merge into SPD-ECN-001 (SPF-ADV-017).
alternatives: Keep single fully allocated ladder;Drop targets entirely;Per-grant instead of per-account targets
rationale: SPF-CLR-001/002: the ladder as written is unsourced at the top and contradicted at the bottom.

question: Is the staffing minimum stated as headcount or as roster coverage by role and day?
recommendation: Roster coverage (UNB-SMP-CLR-001); withdraw "below 6-8" as a target.
alternatives: Adopt 6-8;Adopt 8-10;Adopt ~10 from operations review
rationale: SPF-CLR-003: five inconsistent floors; mis-citation.

question: In what order and by when are the 41 provisional decisions confirmed, and which block production activation?
recommendation: Order by downstream dependency count and irreversibility; accounting set confirmed together before first audited year; all production activation gated by UNB-SMP-CLR-002.
alternatives: Gate only the five opinion-dependent features;Confirm in ID order
rationale: SPF-CLR-004.

question: What operating model applies if counsel answers RCD-005 Q1 negatively or narrowly (no Tier-1 policy approval)?
recommendation: Pre-define the fallback: human approval with AI-prepared dossiers and batch sign-off by an authorized officer within DoA limits; recompute staffing and economics before launch.
alternatives: Proceed and seek opinion later;Delay launch
rationale: SPF-CLR-008: R1 and R8 presuppose Tier 1.

question: Where does the hold registry live in release 1?
recommendation: Separate schema and database role inside the single R1 sponsor database, same HoldPublicationVersion contract; physically separate only when a second sponsor arrives, after TB-02.
alternatives: Separate platform database from day one;Per-sponsor copies with replication
rationale: SPF-ARX-001/002: removes an untested cross-database SPOF with no R1 beneficiary while keeping the seam.

question: Is the protective emergency plane second durable store (REQ-X-047) built for release 1?
recommendation: Defer until TB-07 shows the managed primary cannot meet declared RTO/RPO.
alternatives: Build in R1
rationale: SPF-ARX-003.

question: Are cross-sponsor shadow evaluation and staged rollout of default packs required, and from when?
recommendation: Required before the second sponsor adopts any pack (RR-UNB-RULE-019-r1); per-parameter ordering or enumerated alternatives defined in R1.
alternatives: Per-sponsor simulation only;Simultaneous activation
rationale: SPF-EDF-003.

question: On a shared platform serving several sponsors, may one pool of decision staff exercise A3+ authority (exception grants, gift acceptance, treasury exceptions, sanctions) for many sponsors, and if so under what appointment, conflict and concentration rules?
decision_owner: Sponsor counsel + each sponsor board (platform GC consulted)
recommendation: DECIDED (provisional, product owner, 2026-11-24): no team or person may exercise legally reserved (A3+) authority for more than one sponsor. Every sponsor decides with its own people. Under SPD-ADV-004 those people are always the sponsor's own: Unbound supplies software, not deciders. A third-party administrator using Unbound may prepare work for several sponsors but never holds A3+ authority (UNB-SMP-ORG-003). Option (c), board-appointed shared agents, is rejected (SPR-ADV-008); operator-supplied decision teams are deferred as a hook (SPR-ADV-009).
alternatives: (a) Pooled operator staff decide for all sponsors (rejected, SPR-ORG-004);(c) Board-appointed shared agents (rejected, SPR-ADV-008);(b) Per-sponsor teams (chosen); operator-supplied dedicated teams deferred (SPR-ADV-009)
rationale: The executed variant shows a $46-49 per account P50 swing at OM3 depending on this answer (SPF-ADV-001); the governance passes already lean to (b)/(c) while the economics assumes (a). Re-run executed on the decided answer (model/decision_teams.py): OM3@1M P50 $124.61 pooled -> $146.91 operator-dedicated / $142.26 self-staffed [D]; OM4@1M $29.43 -> $38.62 [D]. Counsel should still confirm the appointment form for operator-dedicated principals (SPD-ORG-002); the decision is stricter than the legal minimum, so it does not weaken any obligation.

question: May a sanctions false-positive disposition made by one sponsor's authorised officer be relied on by another sponsor's screening (RR-UNB-EXT-004-r2)?
recommendation: No by default: reuse scoped to the disposing sponsor legal entity; cross-sponsor reliance only with counsel approval, a recorded reliance event per relying sponsor, and invalidation propagated to all relying sponsors.
alternatives: (a) Platform-wide reuse; (b) per-sponsor reuse (recommended default); (c) platform-wide reuse limited to list-entry versions with counsel-approved criteria
rationale: OFAC liability and the sanctions decider role are per sponsor; R1 has one sponsor so the default costs nothing now.

question: While Unbound keeps the sponsor's DAF program ledger without a SOC 1 report (SPD-PLT-001), how will the sponsor's external auditor obtain assurance over Unbound's IT general controls, and who bears that cost?
recommendation: Ask the sponsor's auditor before R1 build which evidence it will accept (direct testing vs SOC 1 Type I/II); record the resulting audit cost in the bearer map; plan SOC 1 Type II before any second sponsor.
alternatives: (a) Direct auditor testing each year (cost to sponsor); (b) SOC 1 Type I at go-live; (c) SOC 1 Type II from first full year
rationale: Deferring the report is not elimination if the work moves to the sponsor's audit fee (SPF-ADV-020).

question: What standing do Clarity and EDF evaluations have in the requirements gate, and what independent (non-same-model) validation is required before their conclusions are relied on?
recommendation: Treat both as evaluation vocabulary, not gates; require at least one human or different-model review of any conclusion that changes a P0/P1 requirement.
alternatives: Make Clarity or EDF a formal gate; ignore both
rationale: Clarity's own held-out benchmark shows no accuracy gain; EDF's incremental value is unestablished; all passes are one model family.

question: Is Unbound a software platform only, or does it also operate DAF programs (supplying staff, decisions or a sponsoring charity)?
recommendation: DECIDED (provisional, product owner, 2026-11-24): software platform only for now. Unbound builds, hosts and supports the software. The organizations that use it (a sponsor directly, or a third-party administrator acting for sponsors) employ everyone who does human work. Hooks are kept so Unbound can later add operator services (supplied staff, managed service or an affiliated sponsoring charity) without re-design: party types and staffing models in the authority model (UNB-SMP-ORG-003) and extensible fee components (UNB-SMP-ECN-004).
alternatives: Operate programs with Unbound staff (deferred);Affiliated sponsoring charity with branded programs, as Ren does with Renaissance Charitable Foundation (deferred)
rationale: Executed re-run (report 24): Unbound's own modelled cost is about $20.99 per account at OM3@1M (licence floor $10.96 per account plus $52,000 per sponsor). The customer's total DAF operating cost is $138.15 per account, of which $118.05 is the customer's own. Industry servicers vet and prepare but leave final decisions to the sponsor (daf-landscape research on Ren).
